topic.name: Solving Second-Order ODEs Using Laplace Transforms

question.text: Find the Laplace transform of $y(t),$ if \[ y'' + 4y =4\cos{2t}, \quad y(0) =1 , \quad y'(0)=0. \]
question.explanation:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

\begin{align} \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' +4 y \right\} &= \mathcal{L}\left\{4\cos{2t}\right\} \\[3pt] \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' \right\}+4 \mathcal{L}\left\{ y \right\} &= 4\mathcal{L}\left\{\cos{2t}\right\} \end{align}

Let's introduce $\mathcal{L}\left\{ y \right\}=Y(s).$

To calculate $\mathcal L\left\{y''\right\},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a second derivative:

\[ \mathcal{L}\left\{y'' \right\} = s^2 \mathcal{L}\{ y \} - s y(0) - y'(0) = s^2 Y(s) - s y(0) - y'(0) \]

Taking into account the given initial conditions, we get

\[ \mathcal{L}\left\{y'\right\} = s^2 Y(s) - s . \]

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result: \[ \mathcal{L}\left\{ \cos{2t} \right\} = \dfrac{s}{s^2+4} \]

Therefore, we can solve for $ Y(s)\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align} \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' \right\}+4 \mathcal{L}\left\{ y \right\} &= 4\mathcal{L}\left\{4\cos{2t}\right\} \\[5pt] (s^2 Y(s) - s) + 4Y(s) &=4\left(\dfrac{s}{s^2+4}\right) \\[5pt] (s^2+4)Y(s) &=s+ \dfrac{4s}{s^2+4} \\[5pt] (s^2+4)Y(s) &= \dfrac{s^3+8s}{s^2+4} \\[5pt] Y(s) &= \dfrac{s(s^2+8)}{(s^2+4)^2} \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Laplace Transform of a Second-Order ODE

question.text:
Find the Laplace transform of $y(t),$ if

\[ y'' + 2y = \sin{t}, \quad y(0) = 0 , \quad y'(0) = 0. \]
question.explanation:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

\begin{align} \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' + 2y \right\} &= \mathcal{L}\left\{ \sin{t} \right\} \\[3pt] \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' \right\} + 2\mathcal{L}\left\{ y \right\} &= \mathcal{L}\left\{ \sin{t} \right\} \end{align}

Let's introduce $\mathcal{L}\left\{ y \right\}=Y(s).$

To calculate $\mathcal L\left\{y''\right\},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a second derivative:

\[ \mathcal{L}\left\{y'' \right\} = s^2 \mathcal{L}\{ y \} - s y(0) - y'(0) = s^2 Y(s) - s y(0) - y'(0) \]

Taking into account the given initial conditions, we get

\[ \mathcal{L}\left\{y''\right\} = s^2 Y(s) . \]

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result: \[ \mathcal{L}\left\{ \sin{t} \right\} = \dfrac{1}{s^2 + 1} \]

Therefore, we get

\begin{align} \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' \right\} + 2\mathcal{L}\left\{ y \right\} &= \mathcal{L}\left\{ \sin{t} \right\} \\[5pt] s^2 Y(s) + 2Y(s) & = \dfrac{1}{s^2 + 1} \\[5pt] (s^2 + 2)Y(s) & = \dfrac{1}{s^2 + 1} \\[5pt] Y(s) &= \dfrac{1}{(s^2 + 1)(s^2 + 2)} . \end{align}

example.title: Finding the Laplace Transform of a Second-Order ODE

question.text: Find the Laplace transform $Y(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{y(t)\right\}$ if \[ y''+ 3y' + y = 3\sin{t}, \quad y(0) = -1, \quad y'(0) = 0. \]
question.explanation:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

\begin{align} \mathcal{L}\left\{ y''+ 3y' + y \right\} & = \mathcal{L}\left\{ 3\sin{3} \right\} \\[5pt] \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' \right\} + 3\mathcal{L}\left\{ y' \right\} + \mathcal{L}\left\{ y \right\} &= 3\mathcal{L}\left\{ \sin{t} \right\} \end{align}

To calculate $\mathcal L\left\{ y' \right\}$ and $\mathcal L\left\{ y'' \right\},$ we use formulas for the Laplace transforms of the derivatives and apply the initial conditions:

\begin{align*} \mathcal{L}\left\{ y' \right\} &= sY(s) - y(0) = sY(s) + 1\\[5pt] \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' \right\} &= s^2Y(s) - sy(0) -y'(0) = s^2Y(s) + s \end{align*}

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

\[ \mathcal{L} \{ \sin{t} \} = \dfrac{1}{s^2 + 1} \]

Therefore, we can solve for $Y(s)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \mathcal{L}\left\{ y'' \right\} + 3\mathcal{L}\left\{ y' \right\} + \mathcal{L}\left\{ y \right\} & = 3\mathcal{L}\left\{ \sin{t} \right\} \\[5pt] (s^2Y(s) + s) + 3(sY(s) + 1) + Y(s) & = \dfrac{3}{s^2 + 1} \\[5pt] (s^2 + 3s + 1)Y(s) & = \dfrac{3}{s^2 + 1} - s - 3\\[5pt] (s^2 + 3s + 1)Y(s) & = \dfrac{3 - s^3 - s - 3s^2 - 3}{s^2 + 1}\\[5pt] (s^2 + 3s + 1)Y(s) & = -\dfrac{s(s^2 + 3s + 1)}{s^2 + 1}\\[5pt] Y(s) & = -\dfrac{s}{s^2 + 1} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Laplace Transform of a Second-Order ODE

question.text:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem

\[ y'' - 9y = -8e^{-t}, \quad y(0) = 2, \quad y'(0) = 2 \]

is given by

\[ s^2Y(s) - 2s - 2 - 9Y(s) = - \dfrac{8}{s + 1}. \]
question.explanation:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows:

\begin{align} s^2Y(s) - 2s - 2 - 9Y(s) & = - \dfrac{8}{s + 1} \\[5pt] (s^2 - 9)Y(s) & = 2s + 2 - \dfrac{8}{s + 1} \\[5pt] %(s^2 - 9)Y(s) &= \dfrac{2s^2 + 2s + 2s + 2 - 8}{s + 1}\\[5pt] (s^2 - 9)Y(s) &= \dfrac{2(s^2 + 2s - 3)}{s + 1}\\[5pt] (s^2 - 9)Y(s) &= \dfrac{2(s+3)(s-1)}{s + 1}\\[5pt] %Y(s) &= \dfrac{2(s+3)(s-1)}{(s + 1)(s^2 - 9)}\\[5pt] Y(s) &= \dfrac{2(s+3)(s-1)}{(s + 1)(s - 3)(s + 3)}\\[5pt] Y(s) &= \dfrac{2(s-1)}{(s + 1)(s - 3)} \\[5pt] Y(s) &= \dfrac{1}{s+1} + \dfrac{1}{s-3} \end{align}

which is valid for $s > 3.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get \begin{align} \mathcal{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) &= \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ \dfrac{1}{s+1} + \dfrac{1}{s-3}\right\} \\[5pt] y(t) &= \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{\dfrac{1}{s+1} \right\} + \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{ \dfrac{1}{s-3} \right\}\\[5pt] y(t) & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{e^{-t} + e^{3t}} . \end{align}

example.title: Solving a Second-Order Initial Value Problem Using Laplace Transforms

question.text:
Find $y(t)$ given that the Laplace transform of the initial value problem \[ y''(t) - y(t) = - 6\sin{t}, \quad y(0) = 0, \quad y'(0)=3 \]

is given by

\[ s^2Y(s) − 3 - Y(s) = -6\left( \dfrac{1}{s^2+1}\right). \]
question.explanation:
Using the transformed equation, we can solve for $Y(s)$ as follows: \begin{align} s^2Y(s) − 3 - Y(s) &= -6\left( \dfrac{1}{s^2+1}\right)\\[5pt] (s^2-1) Y(s) &= 3- \dfrac{6}{s^2+1}\\[5pt] (s^2-1) Y(s) &= \dfrac{3(s^2-1)}{s^2+1}\\[5pt] Y(s) &= \dfrac{3}{s^2+1} \end{align}

which is valid for $s > 1.$

Now, taking the inverse Laplace transform, we get

\begin{align} \mathcal{L}^{-1}(Y(s)) &= \mathcal{L}^{-1}\left\{\dfrac{3}{s^2+1}\right\} \\[5pt] y(t) &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3\sin{t}}. \end{align}
